question.worked_solution:
We recognize that the series looks similar to the Maclaurin expansion for $f(x)=\operatorname{cos}⁡x.$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡x=1-\frac{{x}^{2}}{2!}+\frac{{x}^{4}}{4!}-⋯+\frac{(-1)^{n}\,{x}^{2n}}{(2n)!}+⋯\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $x=\frac{4\pi }{3}$ into our Maclaurin expansion gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{4\pi }{3}) & =1-\frac{{(4\pi /3)}^{2}}{2!}+\frac{{(4\pi /3)}^{4}}{4!}-⋯+\frac{(-1)^{n}\,(4\pi /3)^{2n}}{(2n)!}+⋯ \\ -\frac{1}{2} & =1-\frac{{(4\pi /3)}^{2}}{2!}+\frac{{(4\pi /3)}^{4}}{4!}-⋯+\frac{(-1)^{n}\,(4\pi /3)^{2n}}{(2n)!}+⋯\,.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, the sum of the series is $-\frac{1}{2}.$
